stem:
Meena's village in Rajasthan gets some rain every monsoon, and rainwater seeps into the ground. Yet the water level in the village well has fallen over the last five years.
Which statement best explains why the groundwater can decrease even though water seeps into the ground?

options.text: Groundwater is an endless underground store, so the well level only appears to fall and will rise again on its own.
More water is pumped out for homes and farms than is replaced by seepage, and new concrete surfaces reduce the rainwater that soaks in.
Seepage adds water to the ground, so the groundwater level must always rise whenever it rains.
Water in wet soil is not groundwater, so the rain that seeps in can never affect the well level.

teacher.key_rationale: Groundwater falls when extraction exceeds replenishment; pumping for domestic and farm use plus concreted surfaces reducing infiltration lowers the water table despite monsoon seepage. Options A, C and D each express a stated-condition or scope misconception consistent with the target traps.
